why: LIT-01 measures real fly joint angular velocities from this recording. Vendored so the measurement reproduces offline and without unpickling.

source.citation: Wang-Chen, S., Stimpfling, V. A., Lam, T. K. C., Ozdil, P. G., Genoud, L., Hurtak, F. & Ramdya, P. (2024). NeuroMechFly v2: simulating embodied sensorimotor control in adult Drosophila. Nature Methods 21(12), 2353-2362. doi:10.1038/s41592-024-02497-y

conversion.to: npz: joint_angles_rad (42, 2000) float64, joint_names (42,), timestep_s scalar
conversion.lossless: verified by exact array comparison after round-trip
conversion.modification: none to the values; rows sorted by joint name for a stable layout

recording.caveat: ONE fly, ONE second, ONE behaviour. This is normal-behaviour speed, not a physiological ceiling, and says nothing about between-animal variation.
